Commentary.Commentary: Back for the chase. Sahibzada Farhan and Saim Ayub to open for Pakistan. Maheesh Theekshana to bowl first.
...THE CHASE

At 22/2, Sri Lanka were staring down the barrel of a collapse. However, Dhananjaya de Silva and Charith Asalanka refused to blink, steadying the ship. It was a decent recovery, but far from dominant at that stage, Pakistan likely felt they held the upper hand, however, the middle overs and the death-overs finish belonged entirely to the hosts. The complexion of the game shifted dramatically thanks to a late-inning blitz from Dasun Shanaka and Janith Liyanage, who combined for a 50-run partnership off only 14 deliveries. Shanaka led the charge with a strike rate of 377, scoring 34 off 9 balls and clearing the ropes five times, three of which came consecutively against Wasim. Janith Liyanage’s clinical 22 off 8 ensured the momentum never dipped, propelling Sri Lanka to a formidable total. Can the visitors match the task? Stay tuned to find out.

In a match where time was a luxury they didn’t have, Sri Lanka played with an audible intent, choosing courage over caution and the scoreboard reflected that bravery. In a frantic 12-over sprint, the narrative shifted with every delivery. Pakistan won the toss and followed the conventional logic of a shortened contest by electing to bowl first. Early on, that decision looked like a masterstroke. They found the breakthroughs they craved and seemed to have the game under a tight leash, but they hadn't accounted for Sri Lanka’s ability to transform a shaky foundation into a stormy finish. From a precarious start, the hosts surged to a massive 160/6.

A massive 24 runs off the final over sees Sri Lanka finish on a high! In this must-win clash to level the series, the batters have delivered an excellent performance. Now, the pressure shifts to the bowlers to defend the total and do their job.
FOUR! Ends with a boundary! A full toss yet again, well outside off. Janith Liyanage slashes it over point and it rolls to the fence. 24 runs off the last over. Sri Lanka end with 160/6.

The atmosphere is electric, and with the weather looking to hold up, we are set for a cracking contest. Can the Sri Lankan lions roar back to square the series, or will Pakistan’s top-order blitz prove too much to handle once again? The toss is just moments away, so get ready for an exciting finish to this T20 series!

Sri Lankan skipper Dasun Shanaka has called for his team to 'hunt as a pack' after a batting collapse in the opener. The management will be hoping for a much-improved display, potentially bringing the slinging Matheesha Pathirana back into the attack to partner with the in-form Wanindu Hasaranga. On the other side, Pakistan might look to test their bench strength ahead of the T20 World Cup, with speedster Naseem Shah possibly sneaking into the XI to add some extra heat to an already dangerous bowling unit.

Hello and welcome to the Rangiri Dambulla International Stadium for the third and final T20I between Sri Lanka and Pakistan. After a frustrating washout in the second game, it all comes down to this high-stakes showdown. Pakistan currently holds a 1-0 lead, meaning the Men in Green have already avoided a series defeat, but they will be hungry to seal the trophy outright. For the hosts, it’s a do-or-die situation. They must win today to level the series and restore some pride on home soil.
...MATCH DAY...

Rain and Sri Lanka have long been reluctant partners in crime, and whenever cricket visits this part of the world, that combination has a habit of gatecrashing the party. The second T20I fell victim to it, despite having plenty riding on the contest, with both Sri Lanka and Pakistan treating the series as a dress rehearsal for the mega event in February. For now, there is little to add except a hope that the rain gods have already taken their offering and allow the final game to go ahead. Looking back at the key takeaways, the talking points remain familiar for the hosts. Sri Lanka were found wanting in all three departments in the opening game, and time is now very much against them. Intent and energy were noticeably missing, and addressing that will be as important as any tactical change. As far as Pakistan are concerned, the picture is far more settled. They ticked most boxes in the first game and looked well-prepared, even if a few moments in the field suggested there is always room for fine-tuning. Both sides could look for a few changes, with experimentation still very much in focus. Pakistan may hand opportunities to the likes of Naseem Shah and Usman Khan as they look to get more game time into the squad, while Sri Lanka could also shuffle their bowling options. Dunith Wellalage, Matheesha Pathirana and Eshan Malinga are among the names the hosts might consider as they try out different combinations in the final outing. With only one match left to influence the series result, Sri Lanka know this is their final chance to show that the opening defeat was an aberration and they can turn potential into performance. Meanwhile, Pakistan will aim to keep things simple and clinical to end with 2-0. The forecast once again points towards rain, which comes as no real surprise. All that remains now is to stay optimistic and hope the weather finally allows the cricket to take centre stage.
